text: Until the sources name them, the deliverable is assumed to be one chart and one pipeline template in one platform repository, with one values file per service named after the service short name of R4 and carrying exactly the keys name, short, schema, topic, queue and image plus the documented defaults; the api deployment is fixed at 2 pods with no autoscaler, the worker deployment is scaled by KEDA on the service's own task queue rwb-<short> with a floor of 0 and a ceiling and backlog threshold that are values, the resource requests and limits of both tiers are values with platform defaults overridden per service, and both the chart and the template are versioned with a scheme in which a breaking change is a new version that a service repository pins by exact version.
why: The story has to publish, render and test one chart and one template, and no source gives a chart name, a repository, a registry, a pod size, a KEDA threshold, a version scheme or a pinning format; the shape it has to render is fixed by Arch v5 slides 20, 33, 38 and 48 and by R4, but nothing fixes the delivery shape around it.
read: Read as delivery defaults that change no business behaviour and no contract: the chart creates no schema, topic, queue, table or REST surface, the values file carries names and sizes only, the api stays at 2 pods and the worker floor stays at 0, and every per-service size or threshold is a value a service OPS story may override without a chart change.
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions, section 10 Authority, section 11 Data, section 12.9 and section 13 Solution plan
confirm: Solution architect and platform administrator confirm the chart name, the repository, the registry and image naming, the resource defaults, the KEDA floor and ceiling and the version and pinning scheme before the chart is Published.
impact: Low: a different chart name, repository, registry, pod size or threshold changes paths and values and not the rendered shape, the stage list or any acceptance criterion; the 19 services render from one chart either way.

text: Until the sources name them, the pipeline is assumed to run on the bank's existing CI service with the same ten stages for every service (build, unit and contract tests, boundary test, image scan, helm lint and helm template, the migration lint and drift gate of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, then deploy DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD), with one gate per environment approved by the release role, and with the secret scan, the personal-data scan and the approved-dependency check as blocking stages that print a file and a rule and never a value; every credential is a key-store reference resolved at deploy time and the image comes from the bank's own registry.
why: NFR-052 and NFR-054 fix what must be blocked and never fix the toolchain, the stage granularity or the promotion approver, and the story cannot exist without one stage list and one gate per environment; without a fixed toolchain the nine wave 1 services would each pick their own.
read: Read from NFR-052 and NFR-054 as the minimum the pipeline must do, and from Arch v5 slide 38 as the 'golden pipeline' of wave 0; the stages and gates are a default and no stage weakens a check: a service cannot remove, reorder or except a stage, and the migration lint and drift gate are the RWB-PLT-E1044-CON stages and are never reimplemented per service.
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions, section 4 Flow steps 6 to 8, section 11 Data (secret references), section 13 Solution plan and section 14 Validation and messages
confirm: DevOps lead and the platform administrator confirm the CI service, the scanner set, the stage order and the promotion approver of each environment before the canary runs through DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD.
impact: Low: a different CI service or scanner changes the template's syntax and not its stages or its checks; a stricter gate adds a stage and changes no acceptance criterion, and a weaker gate is refused by AC3 and AC4.

why: The legacy index entry for NF-01 holds the title and the group only, with no story file, no AC, no TC and no section, so nothing can be copied verbatim; the story still has to be stated and testable in wave 0, and the disposition cannot change to New because NF-01 is an existing legacy key that the realignment moves rather than creates.

text: The standard layout of a service repository is the six folders api, worker, db/migration, contracts, helm and pipeline, the file template.version at the repository root, and nothing else fixed inside a folder: api and worker are the two deployments of Arch v5 slide 33, db/migration is the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15, contracts holds the OpenAPI 3.1 and AsyncAPI documents the service owns, helm holds the values file of the chart of RWB-PLT-N004-OPS, pipeline holds the gate definitions, and a repository is named for the service short name of Template and Rules §R4, so rwb-case holds the repository of the case service.
why: A repository baseline has to name a layout, and no source in the set names one; the six folders are the smallest set that carries the five things Arch v5 already fixes for every service (an API, a worker, its own schema and migrations, its own contracts and its own chart values), and deriving the repository name from the §R4 short name keeps the naming rule of slide 41 without inventing a convention.
read: Arch v5 slides 20 (every service from one template: Spring Boot, outbox relay, inbox, Temporal worker, codec, OpenTelemetry, contract tests), 33 (API with 2 fixed copies and a worker scaled by KEDA), 38 (service template, one Helm chart, golden pipeline) and 41 (schema rwb_<name>, REST /api/recovery/<name>/v1, topic rwb.<name>.events.v1, queue rwb-<name>); Template and Rules §R4 and §R5.5 DP-15; Business Requirements Program v4 §7 constraint Built on ACE (one service, one repository)
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions, section 11 Data, section 13 Solution plan and section 16 Test cases
impact: The layout check, the boundary rule set and the inventory read the folder names from one list, so adding, renaming or removing a folder changes one list in the template and raises the template version; a service that already holds an extra folder keeps it until its next template upgrade.

text: The branch policy is one protected default branch that only the pipeline writes to, short-lived change branches merged through the pipeline, no direct push to the default branch, one release tag per service release and promotion by immutable image digest; the branch and tag names are values of the template and not part of this story.
why: The story has to fix how a change reaches a repository and how a build is promoted, and no source in the set states a branch policy; a protected default branch with pipeline-only writes is the only form that lets the gate set be enforced for every service, and promotion by digest is what keeps a build identical between environments.
read: Arch v5 slides 33 (the two deployments of a service), 38 (golden pipeline built once in wave 0) and 41 (naming of the service artefacts); NFR-054 (the build pipeline blocks a change that carries a secret, personal data or an unapproved dependency); no source in the set names a branch, a tag or a merge policy
applied_in: Section 4 step 8, section 9 State transitions, section 10 Authority, section 13 Solution plan and section 16 Test cases
impact: If the bank's source-control standard differs, the protected-branch setting, the tag convention and the merge rule change as values of the template and the gates are unchanged; a branch policy that admits a direct push to the default branch would weaken AC2 because a change could land without the gate set.

text: The toolchain is the bank's existing CI engine running the one pipeline definition, with the build and container tooling, the artefact registry, the image registry and the secret, personal-data and image scanners provided as platform services and named as values of the template; this story selects no product and pins no version of one.
why: The gate set can be fixed without naming a product, and the programme already runs a CI engine and the registries it needs; naming a product in a story that no source supports would invent a platform decision, while leaving the toolchain unnamed entirely would leave the pipeline unbuildable.
read: Arch v5 slides 20 (/health and /metrics for the platform), 33 (the two deployments), 38 (golden pipeline as a wave-0 enabler) and 41; NFR-052 and NFR-054; Business Requirements Program v4 §7 constraint Built on ACE and the ACE team dependency; no source in the set names a CI engine, a build tool, a registry or a scanner
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions, section 4 steps 1 and 5, section 13 Solution plan and section 14 Validation and messages
impact: A different CI engine or a different registry changes the pipeline definition and the values that name it, and raises the template version; the eight gates, their order and their findings stay the same, so no acceptance criterion changes.

text: The template version is a semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH recorded in the file template.version at the repository root and read by the first stage of every pipeline run: a change to the layout or to a gate's identity is MAJOR, a change to a gate threshold, a scan rule, a boundary rule or a folder's contents is MINOR, and a documentation or comment change is PATCH; every service repository pins exactly one version, and a template change that touches a repository raises the version before any service takes it.
why: AC5 needs a version that can be compared across 19 repositories and an upgrade that is deliberate, and no source in the set fixes a scheme or a file; a semantic version gives the inventory one field to compare and gives a service team one decision to take, while the file at the root is the only place the pipeline can read before it builds anything.
read: Arch v5 slide 38 (service template and golden pipeline built once in wave 0, then each epic adds only its services); Template and Rules §R5.7 rule 6 (wave 0 platform stories carry the Day-1 work) and §R9; no source in the set names a version scheme or a version file
applied_in: Section 4 step 10, section 7 AC5, section 9 State transitions, section 13 Solution plan and section 16 Test cases
impact: If the programme adopts another scheme, the version file keeps one field and the inventory comparison is unchanged; a rise that is not published before a service takes the change would let two repositories run different gate sets, which is exactly what AC5 and AC2 prevent.

text: The four environments are DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD, all four on the shared ACE AKS cluster and the shared App Gateway, and each environment has its own Temporal cluster with its own persistence database and the namespace rwb-recovery, its own Key Vault holding that namespace codec keys and its service credentials, its own ACE database server with the 19 schemas rwb_<name> and one login per service, and its own PgBouncer pool with a connection cap and a statement timeout per login. The hosts, ingress hosts, subscription, resource group, region pairing, the size of a Temporal cluster and of an ACE database, the pool size, the connection cap, the API and worker replica counts and the key store naming are values held in the environment matrix of the platform repository and are agreed with the platform administrator before the first promotion; the story names none of them and hard-codes none of them.
why: Architecture v5 fixes the shape of an environment, one cluster per environment, a namespace per workbench, one schema and login per service and one pool per login, but states no host, subscription, size, cap or name. The baseline must be installable and testable in wave 0, so the shape is fixed as above and every infrastructure value is kept as a value that the platform administrator owns, which invents no business value, no code, no date and no amount.

impact: No business value changes and no service story is blocked: the story is Day 1 with no build dependency, and the values it leaves open are configuration the platform administrator sets, so a changed host, subscription or size is a values file change and not a story change.

text: DEV holds synthetic data only, SIT and UAT hold masked copies produced by the masking path of the bank and loaded by RWB-ITG-TE004-ITG, and PROD holds production data and receives no copy from a lower environment. The data refresh cadence of DEV, SIT and UAT, the extract that feeds each of them and the retention of a replaced copy are values of the environment matrix, agreed with the platform administrator and the data owner, and no production extract is ever targeted at DEV. NFR-045 names development and user acceptance; the system integration environment is included in the masked class because the integration harnesses of waves 1 to 4 run there.
why: NFR-045 forbids production data in development and requires masked copies in user acceptance, and the integration stories of the same run load a masked copy into SIT and UAT, so the three classes above are the reading that keeps every source consistent. No source gives a cadence, a feed or a retention, so those stay values and are not invented in the story.

text: The DevOps team owns the install, the four values files, the four checks and the promotion stage in DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD, the platform administrator approves the environment matrix, the pool caps, the data class and every promotion through the gate, the ACE database administrator owns the schemas, the logins, the grants and the pools in each environment, the security architect approves the key store layout and the cross-environment refusal tests, and production change enters through the release window with the platform administrator as the approver role. Every right is held by a role and never by a person, and a promotion records the role that approved it.
why: No source states an environment owner or a promotion approver, and the run rules forbid naming a person, so the rights are assigned to the roles that already own the pieces in Architecture v5 and in Template and Rules section R5.3. The assignment only names roles, which keeps the story executable and auditable without inventing an owner.

text: The key store is the Key Vault of the shared platform, one per environment, and every secret is reached by a reference of the form <key store>/<object>/<version> resolved at run time under the service's own workload identity; the object path is per service and the Temporal payload codec key is per namespace (rwb-recovery), both per Arch v5 slides 8, 20, 24, 29 and 35. The Key Vault name, the object path convention and the secret owner role per family, beyond the platform administrator of the key store, are values of the baseline.
why: The slides name the Key Vault as the key store and the codec keys as per namespace, but no source gives the object path convention, the Key Vault name or the owner of a secret family, and the scope table and the key-store policy cannot be written without one convention fixed.

applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions, section 4 steps 2 and 5, section 10 Authority, section 11 Data and section 12.7

text: The rotation interval and the overlap window are configuration values of the baseline with no value in the source set, and the rotation is a scheduled job of the platform pipeline that writes a new key-store version; the consumer reads the current version at run time with no rebuild, the previous version stays readable only for the overlap window and is then disabled, after which a call with the old credential is refused. A secret family with no interval stated follows the platform default once it is published.
why: NFR-052 requires the key store and a rotation without a code release, but no source gives an interval, a window or a rotation mechanism, and the story must still state the behaviour it proves.
read: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 NFR-052; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 20 and 24 (Key Vault and codec keys); no rotation interval, overlap window or rotation mechanism in any source read

impact: The interval and the window are changed as values with no code change; a family that rotates faster than the interval allows is given its own row, and the refusal of the old credential after the window holds either way.

text: A non-secret environment setting stays in the environment variables and the chart values of that environment and does not go to the parameter catalog, because REQ-DRI-010's catalog holds every threshold, limit and name as a business value and the chart already versions a host, a port, a timeout and a log level per environment; no separate configuration service beyond the parameters contract and the reference-data contract is introduced by this story. The configuration key names of those settings are values of the chart and of the source map.
why: REQ-DRI-010 names a parameter catalog and a configuration service, the DP table resolves them to the parameters contract and the reference-data contract of rwb-case, and no source says where a deployment setting such as a host or a timeout is held; the story needs one rule so that a service story does not put a threshold in a chart value or a host in the catalog.
